title: Waacking Tutorial For Beginners | How To Waack - Part 1 | DanceWithAbby

extraction.teacher_style: Abhilash breaks down the movements into clear anatomical pathways and vivid imagery. She maintains an encouraging and upbeat tone while progressively increasing tempo.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction and welcoming viewers to the waacking tutorial series
Explanation of the three main aspects of waacking: waack, punk, pose
Introduction of the single arm roll drill
Detailed breakdown of the right arm roll pathway
Breaking the movement down into smaller picture-by-picture counts
Switching to practice on the left side arm roll
Practicing the arm rolls at a faster medium tempo

cues: Roll your right arm up like that
Hit the back of your shoulder
Extend as much as you can
metaphors: Imagine that there is some dust or there's like a bug on your shoulder
Use the back of the shoulder as a springboard, like giving you a rebound movement
common_mistakes: Going outwards instead of staying very close to the ears
One arm being stronger than the other

steps_taught.name: Single Arm Roll
steps_taught.description: Rolling the arm up, hitting the shoulder, extending up, and rolling forward down

what_works: Breaking movements down into numbered picture positions
Progressive tempo increases from slow to medium

quotes.text: Waack means to strike with force.
Imagine that there is some dust or there's like a bug on your shoulder.
If I were to break the movement into small pictures, it will look like this.
You should train your weaker side more so that both arms look equally graceful.
